pr_body:
This is a collection of fixes:
* dd213a5c180997e8b761ca9f8078c0ba58503a0b: This was a crash I discovered while investigating. Probably not the root cause crash, but a crash nonetheless.
* ba491212afcbafdabc89d88b78f1dc5076dea0c3...0b18ae4ed73cbb15452c7c15aefa0c2671db9605: A collection of fixes to _not_ create the window when we're about to handoff each of the new tabs, panes, to an elevated window. That should prevent us from starting up XAML at all, which should take care of #12169. Additionally, it'll prevent us from restoring the unelevated windows, which should resolve #12190
* The remainder of the commits where fixes for other weird edge cases as a part of this. Notably:
  * ff7259918933067872a14df5b0e3c6f6d7764e57: Autopromote the first `split-pane` to a new tab, in the case that it's preceded with only `new-tab` actions that opened elevated windows. 

#### checklist

* [x] I work here
* [x] Docs are fine
* [x] Closes #12190
* [x] Closes #12169

issue_context.title: Crash opening an elevated profile from the taskbar jumplist
issue_context.body:
### Windows Terminal version

main 7061c54

### Windows build number

10.0.22000.434

### Other Software

_No response_

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an elevated profile.
   ```json
            {
                "colorScheme": "Campbell Powershell",
                "commandline": "\"C:\\Program Files\\PowerShell\\7\\pwsh.exe\"",
                "guid": "{14b805d7-b545-418a-b1e8-1fdccd6197f7}",
                "hidden": false,
                "icon": "ms-appx:///ProfileIcons/pwsh.png",
                "name": "PowerShell (Elevated)",
                "startingDirectory": "%USERPROFILE%",
                "elevate": true
            }
   ```
2. Right click on the terminal icon in the taskbar and select your elevated profile.

### Expected Behavior

Nothing to crash.

### Actual Behavior

The un-elevated copy of terminal, which spawned the elevated one crashes. The elevated copy of terminal starts up successfully and can be used as expected. The call-stack seems to be deep within XAML with the last frame in terminal at the `AppHost` destructor, so my _guess_ would be that the app is closing before the XAML stack is fully initialised, leading to the crash.

comments: That is REALLY weird. Does it pop an error message up at you, or just silently crash? I think I saw something similar in #12142, but the stack was very different.
It just silently crashes. It happens every time too, so at least it's consistent.

Super weird. That's unlike the one I was seeing then. I also saw a different crash, while investigating, which I fixed in dd213a5c1. I don't think that'll fix this one though. 

Here's a question: do you have persisted layouts turned on? Did you build debug or release? I'm just trying to find the right way to repro this.

I don't have persisted layouts turned on and it's a release build.

It's worth clarifying, I have no instances of the terminal open to begin with. I just right click on the taskbar and select the elevated profile. The outline of the un-elevated window pops up and disappears, then I get a UAC window and finally the elevated copy of the terminal.

Welp, I can't get your specific crash to repro. I am gonna try and psychically prevent it though. I'm gonna try to make the terminal not create a window at ALL when it's just being invoked to handoff to an elevated terminal. Hopefully, that should prevent XAML from ever starting, which should prevent this crash. I'll have to do this as a part of the fix for #12190 anyways.

My PC isn't exactly slow (i7-8700, M.2 SSD, 32GB RAM), but I have noticed that it does take a while (comparatively) for threads to start once they've been created. If XAML is creating a load of threads and waiting for things to happen, it may be that they aren't starting up as quick as they do on e.g. your machine.

:tada:This issue was addressed in #12205, which has now been successfully released as `Windows Terminal v1.12.1073`.:tada:
